question: An architect resumed a session this morning expecting yesterday's investigation, but the agent behaved as if starting completely fresh with no memory of prior findings. The team confirms the correct session ID was passed. What should the architect check first?
options: A) Whether the teammate who ran the original session had sufficient tool permissions granted
B) Whether the resume call ran from the same working directory the original session was started in
C) Whether the prompt text used to resume matched the original prompt text exactly
D) Whether the original session had exceeded its maximum turn or budget limit before ending
correct_answers: B) Whether the resume call ran from the same working directory the original session was started in
explanations: Incorrect: tool permissions affect what actions the agent may take within a session, not whether the resume call can locate and load the correct transcript file.

Correct. Sessions are stored under a path keyed by the encoded working directory; resuming from a different cwd looks in the wrong location and silently returns a fresh session, which matches the documented most common cause of this symptom.
Incorrect: resume looks up a session by its ID or name, not by matching the new prompt text against the original prompt, so prompt wording differences do not explain a fresh session appearing.
Incorrect: hitting a max-turns or max-budget limit ends a session with an error result but does not prevent it from being found and resumed later; it doesn't cause a fresh session to appear instead.
